name: Lysosomal Disease with Restrictive Cardiomyopathy
aliases: Lysosomal Storage Disorder with Restrictive Cardiomyopathy

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Lysosomal Disease with Restrictive Cardiomyopathy Diagnostic Criteria

criteria.description: Echocardiographic evidence of restrictive cardiomyopathy with preserved systolic function
Demonstration of deficient lysosomal enzyme activity in leukocytes or fibroblasts
Identification of pathogenic variants in genes associated with lysosomal storage disorders
Histopathological confirmation of lysosomal storage material in myocardial tissue
Presence of systemic manifestations such as hepatosplenomegaly or skeletal abnormalities

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of echocardiographic restrictive cardiomyopathy plus either lysosomal enzyme deficiency or genetic confirmation
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires integration of clinical, biochemical, and genetic data.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Restrictive cardiomyopathy with preserved ejection fraction
searchTerms: stiff heart muscle with normal pumping
heart muscle restriction with good ejection

pathognomonic.symptomName: Intracellular lysosomal storage inclusions in myocardial cells
searchTerms: lysosomal storage deposits inside heart cells
storage material in heart muscle cells

common.symptomName: Exercise intolerance due to cardiac dysfunction
searchTerms: poor exercise tolerance due to heart issues

rare.symptomName: Renal impairment secondary to lysosomal storage
searchTerms: renal impairment linked to storage disease
kidney damage due to cellular storage

rare.symptomName: Recurrent infections due to immune dysfunction
searchTerms: recurrent infections due to immune deficiency
irregular heartbeats not caused by restrictive disease

laboratory: Reduced activity of specific lysosomal enzymes (e.g., alpha-galactosidase, beta-glucocerebrosidase)
Elevated biomarkers of lysosomal storage such as urinary glycosaminoglycans
imaging: Echocardiography showing restrictive filling pattern with normal systolic function
Cardiac MRI demonstrating myocardial infiltration and fibrosis
genetic: Pathogenic mutations in genes encoding lysosomal enzymes or transport proteins (e.g., GLA, GBA)
other: Histological identification of lysosomal storage material in myocardial biopsy specimens

distinguishingFeatures: Positive Congo red staining on biopsy

redFlags: Rapid progression of heart failure symptoms despite standard therapy
Early onset restrictive cardiomyopathy in pediatric or young adult patients
Family history of lysosomal storage disorders or unexplained cardiomyopathy
references: Orphanet Report on Lysosomal Disease with Restrictive Cardiomyopathy, ORPHA:217638
Muenzer J. The mucopolysaccharidoses: a heterogeneous group of disorders with variable pediatric presentations. J Pediatr. 2004
Elliott PM, et al. Diagnosis and management of restrictive cardiomyopathy. Heart. 2008
